name: Dialog
purpose: A decision or a short task that must finish before the page continues.
notFor: Anything the user might want to keep open while working — that is SidePanel
A confirmation that needs no decision — that is Toast
A form long enough to scroll on a laptop — that is a route

anatomy.note: The native element, not a div with role=dialog. Four things come free and are hard to hand-roll: focus trapping, the rest of the page going inert, a cancellable Escape, and the top layer — which is why there is no z-index in this component's CSS.
Referenced by aria-labelledby. Level 2 because the dialog starts a new outline.
Actions in reading order: primary last on the inline end.

onClose.meaning: Escape, backdrop click, or the close button
onClose.note: Required. A dialog that cannot be dismissed is a dialog that traps a keyboard user.

dismissible.note: When false, Escape and the backdrop stop closing it, but the close button stays — removing every exit is never correct.

keyboard.Escape: Closes, unless dismissible is false. Native to <dialog>, cancellable.
keyboard.Tab: Cycles inside the dialog only. Native.
keyboard.Shift+Tab: Cycles backwards inside the dialog only.

attributes.aria-describedby: the body id, when the body is a single statement rather than a form

aria.focus: On open, focus moves to the first focusable element in the body, or the dialog itself if there is none — never to the close button, which invites accidental dismissal. On close, focus returns to the element that opened it; the opener is captured on open, not assumed to still be document.activeElement.
aria.announcements: None. The dialog's own role announces it; a live region on top of that double-announces.

content.title: A question or a noun phrase, sentence case, no trailing period. 'Delete this workspace?'
content.actions: The primary action names the verb: 'Delete workspace', never 'OK'. Cancel is always 'Cancel'.
